comments.content: **Palette color is not stable across restarts.** The inline comment promises "按 key 散列取色，稳定且可区分", but Python's built-in `hash()` for strings is randomized by `PYTHONHASHSEED` on every process start (default behavior since 3.3). The same `provider_key` will be assigned a different `fallback_color` (and therefore a different badge color in the UI) after every restart, contradicting the documented stability. Use a deterministic digest such as `int(hashlib.sha1(pkey.encode()).hexdigest(), 16) % len(PALETTE)` or `zlib.crc32(pkey.encode()) % len(PALETTE)` so colors persist across restarts.

(pkey, name, LOGO_URL.format(pkey),
                 PALETTE[zlib.crc32(pkey.encode()) % len(PALETTE)],
                 name[0].upper(), p.get("api")),

comments.content: **`model_upsert` returns 200 OK with an `{"ok": False, "error": ...}` body when the provider does not exist, which is the only endpoint in this file that does so.** Every other endpoint either returns data or a fallback object — none signal failure via body field. Callers cannot distinguish validation failure from success without inspecting the body and the FastAPI default behavior will hide the error in tools like Swagger / `httpx.get(...).raise_for_status()`. Raise `HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=...)` (importing from `fastapi`) and return the created model, matching the conventional REST contract.

comments.content: **Fallback in `model_get` overwrites the explicitly-set `provider_key=None` via dict spread.** This returns `{"provider_key": "?", ...}` even though the literal `None` a few lines above was clearly intended to convey "no provider attached". The synthetic "?" key then leaks into the frontend, where the `ModelMeta` type (`src/components/EvolutionPanel/types.ts` consumer analog) declares `provider_key: string`, so downstream code may treat "?" as a real provider and attempt to look it up. Either omit the spread and explicitly spell out the fallback fields, or return a sentinel like `provider_key: "unknown"` in one place instead of leaving a hidden override.

ConflictRefused / apply_err recovery path leaves the entry in a logically inconsistent state and the documented "可重试" message is misleading. `entry.status = ProposalStatus::Promoted` and `rewrite_jsonl(&p_path, &proposals)?` run BEFORE `human_apply_one`. When `human_apply_one` returns `Err` (including `ConflictRefused`), the on-disk proposals.jsonl already says `Promoted`, but no lesson was applied and the CR stays Pending. Re-toggling ON will hit the dedup branch (`existing` matches the Pending CR) and re-run `human_apply_one` — which can deterministically fail again with the same ConflictRefused (no chance to clear the foreign-merge target without removing it). The error message says "可重试、停用或删除", but "重试" doesn't recover; only OFF (removes Pending CR, sets status=Rejected) actually closes the loop. Either set `entry.status` only after successful apply (cleanest: move the `entry.status = Promoted; proposals[idx] = entry.clone(); rewrite_jsonl(...)` block to after the `mark_human_applied` success path), or restore `Pooled` on the error path. The user comment "Promoted on disk" is a hard contract — should not precede a fallible operation.

Critical section under `EVOLUTION_STORE_LOCK` is now significantly longer. `human_apply_one` opens DB, takes `DB_WRITE_LOCK`, and calls `apply_one` which performs `store::load_all(conn)?` — a full SQLite scan of the memory table — plus a write/lookup, all while still holding `EVOLUTION_STORE_LOCK`. The auto-apply track (`apply_from_consolidation`, apply.rs:181-340) intentionally narrows its critical sections: it pre-computes embeddings outside the store lock and releases `DB_WRITE_LOCK` between iterations, only re-acquiring `EVOLUTION_STORE_LOCK` briefly for the per-CR append. The new toggle path holds the store lock across the heavy DB scan, which can starve concurrent `evolution_*` panel commands and the auto-apply track. Consider: pre-compute the embedding (already done) AND pre-fetch the foreign-merge target check outside the store lock, then narrow the locked section to a brief RMW of `proposals.jsonl` + `changes.jsonl`. Alternatively, do the apply under `DB_WRITE_LOCK` first, then take `EVOLUTION_STORE_LOCK` for the final jsonl rewrite only (same lock-order discipline as the auto-apply track: DB → store, never the reverse).

Pre-computed embedding from an unlocked read can be stale. `precompute_human_apply_embedding` (line 308) reads proposals.jsonl *before* `lock_evolution_store()` and embeds `entry.suggestion_text`. `human_apply_one` then rebuilds the authoritative `EvolutionProposal` from the entry re-read *under* the lock, and passes the pre-lock embedding into `apply_one`. `apply_one` (apply.rs:64-99) uses the embedding as-is and uses `p.suggestion.text` as the lesson content — it never cross-checks the embedding against the current text. If `suggestion_text` was mutated between pre-read and lock acquisition (concurrent edit path; rare but possible if a proposal rewrite path exists), the stored vector will correspond to the obsolete text. Either (a) re-read the entry under the lock and re-embed if the text differs (costs the ONNX round-trip again on mismatch), or (b) drop the pre-compute optimization and compute the embedding inside the lock using authoritative text — at the cost of a few ms under the store mutex but eliminates the staleness window. Note: `derive` writes proposals.jsonl only at consolidate cadence, so concurrent writes during a user toggle are vanishingly rare in practice; the optimization is mostly defending against pathological cases.

`evolution_get_apply_policy` returns `Result<String, String>` (untyped wire format) while `evolution_set_apply_policy` already validates the input through the typed `ApplyPolicy::from_config_str`. Returning `ApplyPolicy` directly across the Tauri boundary would (a) make the contract symmetric with the setter, (b) eliminate the frontend's need to know the string convention, and (c) let `serde` reject malformed values at the deserialization boundary instead of treating them as "auto = 现状". `ApplyPolicy` already derives `Serialize, Deserialize` (policy.rs:30), so this is a one-line change. Note: the frontend's `EvolutionPanel/types.ts` is updated (+25 lines) for this UI; the typed return would simplify the TS counterpart.

`toggle_inner` is exposed as `pub` solely so the integration test file (`tests/evolution_gov.rs`) can call it. The `#[doc(hidden)]` attribute documents intent but doesn't actually constrain the public API surface — anyone importing the `evolution::panel` module can still call it. Compare with the cleaner sibling kernel `cascade_delete_mem_items` which is `pub(crate)` (line 406). The pattern to use here: `pub(crate) fn toggle_inner` plus a `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "integration-tests"))]` re-export, or simply have the integration test go through the `evolution_toggle_proposal` Tauri command (which is a thin wrapper) so the kernel can be `pub(crate)`. As written, `toggle_inner` is part of the crate's published surface and will appear in rustdoc.

comments.content: Three sequential `cr.clone()` calls in the toggle ON branch: `c.clone()` when matching the existing CR (line 167), `changes.push(cr.clone())` after append_change (line 188), and `changes[pos] = cr.clone()` after `mark_human_applied` (line 245). The clones are O(field_size) — not catastrophic — but they make the borrow flow harder to follow and mask the fact that `cr` is only ever used to drive mutations into `changes`. Cleanest restructure: build an owned `cr` in the `None` branch (no clone), and in the `Some(c)` branch find the index once (`Some(pos)`) and mutate `changes[pos]` in place via `&mut changes[pos]` — avoids both clones and the post-hoc `position()` lookup.

`human_apply_one` ignores the `entry_to_proposal` return-None case for Parameter/Code layers in a way that can never trigger here (the caller already gated on `entry.layer == EvolutionLayer::Policy`), but the helper itself doesn't reflect that. If the layer guard is ever loosened (e.g., to also apply SkillHint lessons in future), the helper currently silently falls back to `Err("无对应提案类别...")` from `toggle_inner` rather than its own error, and the change_id lineage / CR status behavior under that error path is undefined. Two cleaner alternatives: (a) make `entry_to_proposal` return `Result<EvolutionProposal, ...>` with the unsupported-layer error included, so the caller's `?` propagates a typed reason; or (b) split the helper into `policy_entry_to_proposal` and a more general `entry_to_proposal` so each call site has a single clear contract. The current shape works but is mildly confusing.

Race condition: `onApplyPolicyChange` lacks an in-flight guard, unlike the established `setMemoryControl` pattern in `SettingsPage.tsx` which uses `if (configBusy) return;`. With rapid clicks (auto → confirm → auto within the network round-trip), each click captures its own `prev` from current state; if two `evolution_set_apply_policy` invocations interleave, the second one's failure could roll back to a stale `prev` and desync the UI from the backend (e.g. confirm-fails → setState(prev="auto") while the in-flight auto call later succeeds and writes auto anyway, but the rollback already moved state to confirm).

Worse, the radiogroup only disables on `busy` (which is set by `runCmd` for the *other* operations), not during a save in flight — so the user can re-click while a write is pending. Recommend either (a) a `savingPolicyRef` / in-flight flag guarding the function entry, or (b) making the buttons `disabled={busy || savingPolicy}` with a dedicated `savingPolicy` state mirroring `reflecting`.

`decisionBadge` is called inline inside `proposals.map(...)` and walks `changes.filter(...)` for every card — O(proposals × changes) per render. Combined with re-renders on every `busy` toggle and every reflect-now round trip, this can become noticeable once the pool grows (the panel can already have dozens of proposals and a hundred+ changes). Consider memoizing with `useMemo` keyed on `(proposals, changes)` so the badge list is built once per data change, not once per parent render. The priority semantics are pure derivations and benefit from referential stability if downstream components are added later.

The mount-time useEffect issues `evolution_get_apply_policy` and `evolution_metrics` sequentially even though they have no data dependency on each other; running them in `Promise.all` would shave one network round-trip off the first paint of the radiogroup + metrics strip. The two `try/catch` blocks can be merged into one `Promise.allSettled` while still letting each catch swallow its own error (read failures are intentionally silent and independent — policy fails → state stays "auto", metrics fail → strip hidden).

The `APPLY_POLICY_MODES` constant inlines the aria-prefix strings (`应用策略：自动生效`, `应用策略：需我确认`) while the visible label comes from the `APPLY_POLICY_LABEL` map imported from `types.ts`. If either label ever changes, the aria text will silently drift. The sibling pattern in `SettingsPage.tsx` (`AUTO_EXTRACT_MODES`) has the same structure, so this is consistent with the codebase convention — but the convention itself is a small hardcoding smell; consider deriving the aria prefix from a single source (e.g. `"应用策略：" + label`) so the two stay in lockstep.

Segment 2's `for _ in 0..3` retry loop acknowledges a real TOCTOU between `policy::set_apply_policy` (which holds `APPLY_POLICY_WRITE_LOCK` + uses `atomic_write`) and `policy::auto_apply_allowed` (which calls `read_apply_policy_at` with NO lock acquisition — see policy.rs lines 51-70). Two problems with this:
1. The test's retry tolerance (per the comment, "共享目录互踩的既有容忍口径") papers over a production race: another process (U15 llm_integration) writing bot-config.json between this test's set and read can cause `auto_apply_allowed` to return the wrong value. Production callers cannot retry.
2. The retry window is unbounded on failure — each loop iteration reads `bot-config.json` again, so a third writer can keep stomping indefinitely. Suggest `policy::read_apply_policy_at` either (a) acquire a shared lock so concurrent writers are blocked, or (b) read inside the same RMW critical section via a `read_under_rmw_lock()` that takes the write lock to drain in-flight RMW. Either way, the test should not need 3 retries.
`onApplyPolicyChange` 不像同文件 `runCmd` / `onReflectNow` 那样在开始时清掉旧 error/info——成功落盘后，前一次操作的错误 banner 仍然挂在新选中的档位上。补充 `setError(""); setInfo("")` 在 `setApplyPolicy(next)` 之前即可，与文件内同类 handler 对齐。
硬编码 "近30天" 与后端指标中的 `observation_window_days` 解耦——观察窗口未来如果调整（如 observe 侧支持季度/年度窗口），标签会与实际数据不符。建议改为 `metrics.observation_window_days` 拼装。

comments.content: Segment 6 line 260 defines `let now_ms = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp_millis();` which is then reused in segment 7 (line 309) to insert the target memory. While this is logically correct (the operations don't depend on the exact value), the variable name suggests it's local to segment 6's purpose (`from_proposal` uses it only for `expires_at_ms`). Consider either: (a) declaring `now_ms` close to its first use in segment 6, and capturing a fresh `target_now_ms` in segment 7, or (b) renaming to clarify scope (e.g., `seg6_now_ms` and `seg7_now_ms`). The current cross-segment reuse works but is mildly opaque about time semantics across the boundary.

Segment 4 line 229 asserts `lesson.content == proposals[0].suggestion.text`. The test relies on `derive_proposals`'s deterministic `proposal_id` for the `pid` cleanup target, but does NOT assert the exact `suggestion.text` value. If `derive_proposals` changes the contradiction text format (e.g., adds a prefix), this assertion still passes (comparing the changed text against itself), but downstream consumers of the lesson may break. Consider pinning the expected text in an assertion (e.g., `assert!(proposals[0].suggestion.text.starts_with("LLM resolved contradiction"))`) to lock the contract on what gets persisted.
comments.existing_code: assert_eq!(lesson.content, proposals[0].suggestion.text);

comments.content: Redundant work on dedup-Active path: when dedup matches an existing Active CR and human_apply_one returns AlreadyPresent (the most common case for re-toggling an already-active proposal), this block does changes[pos] = cr.clone() + rewrite_jsonl for no actual state change (mark_human_applied is a no-op on Active). Additionally, the entire policy branch above is wasted I/O — human_apply_one performs a full SQLite scan (store::load_all) and opens a DB connection for a guaranteed AlreadyPresent outcome. Consider short-circuiting after dedup match when existing CR is already Active (with optional recovery path if lesson was lost from DB). This wastes I/O on every re-toggle after the first one.
